provenance.construction: Symplectic halving (mirror fold) of the board's CSS entry codes/960-24-40.json ([[960,24,40]], by @MicheldeMessieres), a weight-6 two-block group-algebra (2BGA) code over C24 x Dic5 (construction of arXiv:2306.16400, Lin and Pryadko). The fold uses a fixed-point-free involution tau of the parent's qubits that maps the X-check rowspace onto the Z-check rowspace: tau(1,g) = (2, h * psi(g)) with h = z^3x^2y^1 and psi the automorphism z -> z^5, x -> x^4, y -> z^12x^1y^3; tau(2, h * psi(g)) = (1, g) (elements indexed as in the parent); block 1 = parent qubits 0..479, block 2 = 480..959. Fold qubit i is the pair {q_i, tau(q_i)}, q_i the i-th smallest qubit with q_i < tau(q_i). Each parent X-check row gives one generator: X on the pairs whose q_i is in the row, Z on the pairs whose tau(q_i) is in the row. S = (A|B) is isotropic, k = 24/2 = 12, check weight 6, not CSS under any local Clifford.
provenance.notes: Derived from codes/960-24-40.json by @MicheldeMessieres (a weight-6 two-block group-algebra (2BGA) code over C24 x Dic5 (construction of arXiv:2306.16400, Lin and Pryadko)). The halving/doubling correspondence is the board's fieldnote fieldnotes/2026-09-28-symplectic-doubling-and-halving.md (@MathysRennela; Prop. 4 of arXiv:2609.30069) and the abelian mirror-code construction of Khesin and Lu (arXiv:2603.05496); the fold convention and the mirror shape are those of @MicheldeMessieres's codes/452-115-18.json and codes/336-10-28.json. Our part, stated narrowly: we enumerated the block-swapping mirrors tau(1,g) = (2, h psi(g)^(+-1)) over every automorphism psi of the group and every h, grouped the folds by the verifier's WL signature, and searched each class. Instruments and depths (lightest Pauli weight found): central-orbit, rung 1, seed 51, 7 partitions x 4000 trials: 36; central-translation pool, rung 1, seed 51, 20 calls x 4000 trials: 65; parent-quotient pool, rung 1, seed 51, 240 calls x 4000 trials: 36; central-orbit, rung 2, seed 52, 7 partitions x 100000 trials: 36; parent-quotient pool, rung 2, seed 52, 540 calls x 20000 trials: 36; ci-plain-doubling, rung ci, seed 52, 2000000 trials: 42. Distance d = 36 is the Pauli weight of the lightest logical any method found: a witness-backed upper bound, not an exact certificate. Construction and literature novelty are not claimed. Distance revised on 2026-10-28 by @MinboGaoTHU using an independently checked weight-34 Pauli logical from parent-symmetry witness transfer, retaining upper-bound confidence.
